response: **VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The component provides a solid foundation with proper native button controls, `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, and roving `tabIndex`. However, it exhibits critical design breakdowns in ARIA relationship bindings (`aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`) and focus management during keyboard arrow navigation (`setActiveTab` is updated on arrow press, but DOM `.focus()` is never dispatched to the newly activated tab). --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions - *Predicted*: Missing bidirectional relationship links (`aria-controls` from tab to panel, `aria-labelledby` from panel to tab). - *Predicted*: Keyboard arrow navigation alters state (`activeTab`) without shifting programmatic focus (`element.focus()`), leaving the virtual cursor or keyboard focus stranded on the previously active tab. - *Predicted*: Screen reader badge announcement issues (badge count run together with tab label). - *Outcome*: All three predictions confirmed upon reading the implementation. --- ### Critical Findings (blocks access) *No complete blockers or total keyboard traps identified.* --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) 1. **Arrow navigation updates active state but fails to move DOM focus** - **Location**: `handleKeyDown` in `ProductTabs` (lines 7–31) - **Pattern / WCAG**: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern (Keyboard Interaction) & WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard - **Impacted Group**: Keyboard-only users and Screen Reader users - **Why this matters**: In an automatic activation model (where arrow keys switch tabs), moving focus to the new tab is required so that subsequent Tab key presses enter the newly active tab panel. As written, pressing ArrowRight changes `activeTab`, but DOM focus remains on the old tab button. When the user hits Tab, focus jumps to the next interactive element relative to the old tab rather than navigating smoothly into the active panel. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: Call `.focus()` on the newly selected element inside the switch branch or via a `useEffect` keyed on `activeTab`: ```jsx const selectTab = (newIndex) => { setActiveTab(newIndex); tabRefs.current[newIndex]?.focus(); }; ``` 2. **Missing bidirectional bindings (`aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby`)** - **Location**: Tab element line 41 (`button`) and Panel element line 60 (`div[role="tabpanel"]`) - **Pattern / WCAG**: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern & WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - **Impacted Group**: Screen Reader users - **Why this matters**: Screen readers rely on `aria-controls="panel-id"` on `[role="tab"]` to announce which panel is governed by the tab and provide shortcuts to jump directly to that panel. In return, each `[role="tabpanel"]` must have `aria-labelledby="tab-id"` to give the container an accessible name when the user enters it. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Fix**: - On `
